_readme: All heroines, their play styles, cool-meter cracks and story. Edit freely: the game reads this file at start. Stats: speed = paddle top speed (px/s), size = paddle radius (px), reaction = seconds she sees the puck late (higher is easier), aim = how far her aim wanders (px), bank = 0..1 how often she banks shots, aggression = 0..1 how far forward she plays. layers = her cracks: each time her Cool runs out she cracks a little more (expression and pose, never clothing), and that crack's stat drops. Layer effects: speed/size multiply, reaction adds. outfits = cosmetic costumes (no stat effect): unlock 'default', 'story' (finish her story) or 'gems' (bought in the Wardrobe). attitude = what she thinks of you after N wins (0..6). Each match has a 'level': you need that level to play it (story wins earn most of it; pickup games and cups the rest). unlock_wins = story wins needed to meet her; unlock_done = heroines you must win over first. barks = lines she says during a match: 'hostile' for her first two matches, 'warm' after. finale = the championship gauntlet after all four are won over. Every character is an adult. PG-13 build: no nudity, romance stops at a kiss.

prologue.text: The Afterglow: a neon arcade lounge that stays open past three. Last month a bar chain bought it. Tonight they sent their new night manager.
That's you. Your first memo from head office says to shut down the regulars' after-hours game.
So YOU'RE the suit. You towed my bike this morning, by the way.
It was in the fire lane.
And you got the manager job I've been doing for free for two years. Congratulations. Everyone hates you.

Here's the deal. The Last Call League has rules, and everyone on the whiteboard signed them. First to five on the table. Score a power smash and the other player loses their cool. There's a meter. It's very scientific.
Beat us at our own game and maybe the league lets you stay. Lose, and you write head office a letter saying you quit.

Win them over one match at a time. Each win changes what they think of you and unlocks a memory for the album. Across the street, the owner of the Static has heard about league night. And Sable, who founded the Afterglow, is watching.

mila.name: Mila Reyes
mila.tagline: Bike courier. Plays fast, talks faster. You towed her bike.
mila.grudge: You towed her bike on your first morning.
mila.signature_tip: A dead-straight rocket at the middle of your goal. Park your paddle in the centre of the mouth when you see the warning.
mila.perk_text: Win Mila over to learn her Bullet: your smash flies straight at the middle of her goal.

her_goal: Ha! Go back to your spreadsheet.
hostile.crack1: You did NOT just... fine. FINE. I'm still faster.
hostile.crack3: This is not happening. This is NOT happening.

your_goal: Do that again. No, wait, don't.
warm.crack1: Heh. You've been waiting for that one, huh?
warm.crack2: Eyes on the puck. ...Or don't. Your call.
warm.crack3: Okay, you win this round. Mostly.

before.text: Twenty-eight bucks to get my bike out of the impound. I'm taking it out of your dignity.
I'll pay you back if you win.
Oh, I'm winning. And then you're writing that letter.

after.text: No. No way. Best of three!
League rules say one match a night.
Then I'll be back tomorrow. Don't you dare tow anything.

scene.title: Sore Loser
scene.brief: Mila sits on the edge of the table, hair a mess, arms crossed, glaring at you and refusing to admit she's blushing.

before.text: I watched replays of myself all day. I lean left when I panic. Not tonight.
Also I taped my lucky shoelace to my wrist. Strategy.
That's... actually smart.
Don't compliment me. It's weird.

after.text: I leaned left. I leaned SO left.
...You're not totally awful. For a suit. Walk me to my bike? I'm not scared of the dark. I just want a witness.

scene.title: Borrowed Jacket
scene.brief: Outside under the neon sign, Mila wears your oversized work jacket over her racer gear, leaning on her bike, still pretending to be annoyed.

before.text: I brought backup. Every courier in the city is watching tonight.
Six couriers in rain gear crowd the bar, chanting her name and booing yours.
Is that a sign with my face crossed out?
Dex made it. He's very proud. Don't embarrass me in front of my people.

after.text: The couriers go quiet. Then Dex starts a slow clap, and the whole crew joins in.
Traitors. All of them. They're asking if you're single.
...I told them you're terrible. Hands off.

scene.title: Courier Crowd
scene.brief: Mila in her racer gear stands on the table rail, pointing at you in mock outrage while her courier friends cheer offscreen. She's fighting a grin.

before.text: It's pouring. Mila walks in soaked, wheeling her bike. The back tyre is flat.
Don't. Say. Anything.
I have a patch kit in the office.
...Why do you have a patch kit?
I bought one after the towing thing. In case.
That's either really sweet or really creepy. Play me while I decide.

after.text: You patched it while I was drying off, didn't you? It's fixed.
Okay. Sweet. I decided sweet.
Stay till the rain stops? I'm not riding home in this. And I'm keeping this hoodie.

scene.title: Rain Check
scene.brief: Mila sits on the bar in an oversized Afterglow hoodie with a towel round her shoulders, hair dripping, watching you patch her bike tyre on the floor.

before.text: Dex keeps asking when you're coming to courier trivia night. I keep telling him never.
...Because I want you to myself. Forget I said that. Rack the puck.

after.text: Okay, I give up pretending I'm still mad at you. It's exhausting.
Buy me fries. Big ones. We're... whatever we are now.

scene.title: Fries at 4 AM
scene.brief: Mila in her racer gear and your jacket, sharing fries with you on the lounge's back steps at dawn, leaning on your shoulder.

before.text: No jokes tonight. If I win, you buy breakfast for a week.
And if I win?
Then I stop pretending I keep coming back for the hockey.

after.text: Fine. You win. I like you. There, I said it.
Here, have my Bullet. I'll teach you the wrist thing tomorrow. Tonight you're walking me home. The long way.
Halfway down the empty street, she stops, rolls her eyes at herself, and kisses you.

scene.title: The Long Way Home
scene.brief: You and Mila walk her bike down an empty neon street at dawn, her hand in yours. She has just kissed you and is pretending it didn't happen, grinning.

juno.name: Juno Hart
juno.tagline: Bartender. Never hits the puck straight. You took her job.
juno.grudge: You got the manager job she'd been doing for free.
juno.signature_tip: A wall shot that loses no speed on the bounce. Watch which wall she aims at and meet it on the rebound.
juno.perk_text: Win Juno over to learn her Ricochet: your smash banks off the far wall without losing speed.

hostile.crack1: That was a twitch. Not a crack. A twitch.
hostile.crack2: If you say one word, I'm salting your sodas forever.
hostile.crack3: ...Congratulations. You're the worst person I know.

warm.crack1: Mm. That one I let you have.
warm.crack2: You're blushing more than I am. Focus.
warm.crack3: Well. Now we're even on blushing.

before.text: Two years I ran this place. Inventory, payroll, the broken claw machine. Then they send a stranger with a lanyard.
I didn't ask for the job.
Then losing it shouldn't hurt. Straight shots are for people who can't do geometry.

after.text: You read the wall. Nobody reads the wall.
This changes nothing. You're still a lanyard.

scene.title: Behind the Bar
scene.brief: Juno, behind the bar in her vest and bow tie, slams a soda down in front of you, furious, and refuses to admit she lost.

before.text: I've drawn every angle on this table on a napkin. Forty-one napkins.
Is that why we're out of napkins?
Don't. Be. Charming.

after.text: Forty-two napkins, and none of them had you on it.
...I read your memo. You never sent the order to shut us down. Why?
Because this place is the only thing that chain bought that's worth anything.

scene.title: The Memo
scene.brief: Juno, sleeves rolled up, sits on the office desk reading your unsent memo by lamplight, looking up at you differently for the first time.

before.text: Inventory night. You count bottles, I count your mistakes.
Why is there a case of maraschino cherries marked 'emergency'?
Because some nights are emergencies. Rack 'em. Loser counts the limes.

after.text: ...You kept my schedule. The one I made. You didn't change a single shift.
It was a good schedule.
Nobody's ever said that to me. I'm going to need a minute. And the emergency cherries.

scene.title: Stockroom
scene.brief: Juno in her shirt and vest, sleeves rolled up, sits on a stack of soda crates in the stockroom with a clipboard and a pen between her teeth, eating cherries from the jar.

before.text: Head office sent an auditor today. Juno watched you walk him around the lounge.
You told him I built the stock system. And the rota. And the cocktail list.
You did.
You could have taken the credit. That's what lanyards do.
I'm so mad I could kiss you. Play. Now. Before I do something stupid.

after.text: I stole the fancy sparkling cider from the auditor's welcome basket.
Come on. Office. We're celebrating you being a decent human being. It's very rare.

scene.title: Credit Where Due
scene.brief: Juno in her work clothes and your blazer lounges on the office couch, popping a bottle of sparkling cider, laughing as the cork hits the ceiling.

before.text: Proposal. You keep the title, I keep running the place, and we both lie to head office.
Deal. Winner picks who does payroll.

after.text: Fine, I'll do payroll. You'd mess it up anyway.
Stay after close. I'll make you the milkshake that isn't on the menu.

scene.title: Off the Menu
scene.brief: Juno sits on the bar in her bartender vest and your tie, sliding you a glowing neon milkshake with two straws and a small smile.

before.text: Last napkin. It just says: don't fall for the new guy.
So I'd better win, huh?

after.text: I'm keeping that napkin. Framing it, actually.
Here's my Ricochet. The trick is to aim at the wall like you mean it. Like this.
She leans across the bar and kisses you. Behind her, the framed napkin catches the neon.

scene.title: Perfect Angle
scene.brief: Juno leans across the bar to kiss you, eyes closed, smiling into it. The framed napkin reading 'don't fall for the new guy' hangs on the wall behind her.

kat.name: Kat Vance
kat.tagline: Owns the Static, the dive bar across the street. Your league night stole her crowd.
kat.grudge: Your chain's league night flyers stole her Thursday crowd, and one ended up taped to her door.
kat.signature_tip: Leaves slow and keeps speeding up. Step up and meet it before the centre line, while it's still slow.
kat.perk_text: Win Kat over to learn her Slingshot: your power shot leaves slow and speeds up all the way to her goal.

her_goal: Slow start, big finish. Like me.
hostile.crack1: Those were my lucky shades. I own nine. Keep dreaming.
hostile.crack2: I dropped my pick! Nobody saw that!
hostile.crack3: ...This never happened. Nobody across the street hears about this.

her_goal: That one had extra spin, just for you.
warm.crack1: Keep my shades warm for me, champ.
warm.crack2: Like the band? I'll play you the record. Later.
warm.crack3: Stop smiling at me like that. I'm trying to lose with dignity.
warm.signature: Wait for it... wait for it...

before.text: A woman in a leather jacket slams the door open and slaps a crumpled flyer on the bar.
'LEAGUE NIGHT AT THE AFTERGLOW. THURSDAYS.' This was taped to MY door. Thursday is MY night.
Head office did the flyers. I just...
Kat Vance. I own the Static. My regulars are drinking HERE now. So I'm joining your stupid league.
I win, the flyers stop. You win... you won't.

after.text: That table's tilted. That's the only explanation.
It's not tilted. I level it every Monday.
Then I'm coming back next Thursday. And the one after. Until it's tilted my way.

scene.title: Wrong Bar
scene.brief: Kat stands at the table in her band tee and jeans, leather jacket slung over one shoulder, jabbing a finger at you, furious and flushed.

before.text: I've been practising on the Static's table. It's older than you and it has a dead spot in the corner.
If I can beat THAT table, I can beat you.
Why not just get a new table?
With what money? Somebody stole my Thursdays.

after.text: ...Okay. It's not the table. It's you. You're annoyingly good.
What if the Static hosted league night on Mondays? We're closed Mondays.
...You'd send people to my bar? Why would you do that?
Because the league's better with two bars.

scene.title: Dead Spot
scene.brief: Kat in her band tee and ripped jeans sits on the bar of the empty Static across the street, its old table behind her, arms folded, studying you suspiciously.

before.text: Monday. The Static is packed for its first league night. Kat looks terrified.
There are forty people in my bar. I haven't had forty people in my bar since the Super Bowl.
Play me first. Make it look good. If I lose in front of them, I'll still kill you.

after.text: They're buying drinks. They're buying SO many drinks.
You did this. I hate it. I mean I love it. I mean... shut up and have a root beer. On the house.

scene.title: Monday Night
scene.brief: Kat behind the bar of the packed Static in her band tee and jeans, pulling two pints at once and laughing, the crowd a neon blur behind her.

before.text: I got my band back together for the Static's Monday nights. We play after league.
Our drummer quit. So, unrelated question: can you keep a beat?
Is that a job offer?
It's a dare. Beat me first.

after.text: You can't drum. That's fine. Nobody can drum.
Stay for soundcheck anyway. I want someone to watch who isn't Juno judging my bass.

scene.title: Soundcheck
scene.brief: Kat on the Static's tiny stage in her band tee and jeans, bass guitar slung low, grinning at you over the mic stand under red stage lights.

before.text: I found something out. The flyer on my door? You didn't tape it there. Head office did.
You took the blame for two months and never said a word.
You needed someone to be mad at.
That's the most annoying, decent thing anyone's ever done for me. Play me before I cry.

after.text: I tore up the flyer. Kept one piece. The bit with your chain's logo, so I can throw darts at it.
Walk me home? It's across the street, I know. Walk slow.

scene.title: Across the Street
scene.brief: Kat in her band tee and your work jacket stands in the middle of the empty street between the two bars at 4 AM, both neon signs glowing behind her, reaching for your hand.

before.text: No trash talk tonight. I keep starting sentences and they come out nice. It's horrible.
So here's the bet. I win, you play bass in my band forever. You win...
I win?
You win, you get a dance. One slow song, on the Static's stage, after close. Don't make it weird.

after.text: Okay. You win. One dance. Mind the stage, it's older than the table.
And take my Slingshot. Start slow, finish strong. Like I said. ...Like this song.
The song ends. Neither of you moves. Then she kisses you, and the amp hums along.

scene.title: Last Song
scene.brief: Kat and you slow-dancing alone on the Static's stage after close, her forehead against yours, her bass leaning on the amp, red stage lights turned low.

sable.name: Sable Marchetti
sable.tagline: Founded the Afterglow, sold it to your chain. Undefeated for six years.
sable.grudge: You're the face of the company that bought her lounge.
sable.signature_tip: Leaves wide and curls back into your goal. Don't chase where it starts; cover where it bends to.
sable.perk_text: Win Sable over to learn her Hook: your smash curls into the goal from a wide angle.
sable.unlock: Win over two of the others (all 6 of their matches)

her_goal: Is that all the company sent?
hostile.crack1: Nobody has cracked my poker face in six years. Enjoy it. Once.

warm.crack1: Go on. You've earned a smile.
warm.crack2: My hands are shaking. Your fault.
warm.crack3: I don't lose. I just... let you have tonight.
warm.signature: Can you read the curve yet?

before.text: I built this place with my own hands. Sold it to keep the lights on. And they sent you to tidy up what's left.
My regulars like you now. I don't. Show me why I should.

after.text: Six years. Six years nobody has seen me sweat.
Don't get comfortable. That was a warm-up.

scene.title: First Sweat
scene.brief: Sable leans back on the table, blazer over one shoulder and a strand of hair out of place, eyes narrowed, studying you like a problem she plans to destroy.

before.text: I closed early tonight. No audience.
Whatever happens on this table stays between us. I sent the regulars home.

after.text: ...My hands are shaking. That hasn't happened since my first tournament.
Juno told me about the memo you never sent. Come up to the office. We should talk.

scene.title: The Office
scene.brief: Sable in her old office in her velvet blazer, lit pink by the neon sign through the window, pouring two cups of tea.

before.text: I found the box. Opening night, nine years ago. Photos, the first menu, the original sign.
Win, and I'll show you. Lose, and it goes back in the closet with my feelings.

after.text: That's me, twenty-two, with a borrowed table and a terrible haircut.
...I never wanted to sell. I want you to know that. I want someone to know that.
Then let's get it back.

scene.title: Opening Night
scene.brief: Sable, blazer off and sleeves rolled up, sits on her office floor surrounded by old photos of the Afterglow's opening night, laughing at one of them, eyes a little wet.

before.text: Head office wants to turn the Afterglow into a sports bar. Big screens. Wings. No table.
Over my dead lanyard.
Good answer. Show me you'll fight for it.

after.text: You fight dirty. I like that in a co-conspirator.
Roof. Now. I think better up there, and you're not saying no.

scene.title: Rooftop
scene.brief: Sable wrapped in your coat sits on the roof ledge beside the buzzing neon sign, city lights behind her, twirling a lollipop like a cigar.

before.text: I've decided I'm buying the Afterglow back. With your help, my spy inside head office.
But I don't partner with people I can beat. Prove it again.

after.text: Partners, then. Fifty-fifty. I'll even let you keep the lanyard.
Head office will sell if we can prove this place makes money. One big night. The Last Call Championship.
Partners celebrate. Pancakes. My treat.

scene.title: Partners
scene.brief: Sable in her velvet blazer sits on the edge of her desk signing a napkin contract, pulling you closer by your tie with a sly smile.

before.text: For the title. Winner's name goes at the top of the wall.
And me. Win or lose, honestly. But don't tell the others I said that.

after.text: New champion. Your name goes on the wall tomorrow.
And the Hook is yours. One more thing. Champion's privilege.
She pulls you in by the lanyard and kisses you under the neon sign.

scene.title: Champion's Privilege
scene.brief: Sable kisses you under the Afterglow's neon sign beside the championship table, her blazer around your shoulders, your name freshly painted at the top of the wall behind her.

before.text: Championship night. Head office agreed: if the Afterglow sells out tonight, Sable can buy it back.
Every ticket's gone. The Static's sold out too. Kat's running a screen over there.
There's a line round the block. I made a mocktail called The Lanyard. It's mostly regret and grapefruit.
Couriers on the roof, couriers on the bar. Dex brought a drum.
League rules: the champion has to beat all four of us. Back to back. No breaks.
In front of everyone?
In front of everyone. Last call, partner. Make it count.
First up! No mercy, no breakfast bets. Just the Bullet.
I drew this match on a napkin. You lose on it. Prove the napkin wrong.
Half the Static's watching on a screen. Don't make me look bad. Or do. Either way.
Six years undefeated, until you. Let's see if it was a fluke.

after.text: The lounge explodes. Someone shakes up a soda. Dex's drum breaks.
We did it. Head office signed the papers ten minutes ago. The Afterglow's ours.
Ours. As in, I'm a co-owner now? I want that in writing. On a napkin.
Does this mean I get free fries forever?
The Static's officially the Afterglow's sister bar. We're making T-shirts.
Last call, everyone. Not you four. You five. Group photo. Now.
The flash goes off. Five people, one table, and a torn SOLD banner. Best photo on the wall.

scene.title: Afterglow
scene.brief: Dawn after the championship: you and all four heroines crowd around the championship table under the neon sign for a group photo. Mila on the rail, Juno holding a napkin, Kat with her bass, Sable holding the deed, the 'SOLD' banner torn in half on the floor.
